title: Symmetric operadic mapping cylinder with relative restriction and active-slice comparison
statement:
Use the conventions of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family] for symmetric operads, families, coherent functors and active cocones, categorical equivalences of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], and cocartesian fibrations and edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $P^\otimes$ and $Q^\otimes$ be small symmetric infinity-operads, let $O^\otimes$ be a symmetric infinity-operad in a containing universe, and let $P^\otimes\xrightarrow{u}Q^\otimes\xrightarrow{v}O^\otimes$ be maps of symmetric infinity-operads. All functor categories below are formed in a containing universe; the constructed cylinder is small in the universe of $P^\otimes$ and $Q^\otimes$. Set
$$S_u=(P^\otimes\times\Delta^1)\amalg_{P^\otimes\times\{1\}}Q^\otimes,$$
with its map to $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^1$ and its map to $O^\otimes$ given by $vu$ on the cylinder and by $v$ on $Q^\otimes$. There exist a small correspondence $\pi:M_u^\otimes\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^1$, a family map $g:M_u^\otimes\to O^\otimes$, and a degreewise injective categorical equivalence $j:S_u\to M_u^\otimes$ over both bases, identifying the endpoint fibers exactly with $P^\otimes,Q^\otimes$. The projection $t:M_u^\otimes\to\Delta^1$ is a cocartesian fibration in the sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and for every vertex $p$ of $P^\otimes$ the edge $j(\{p\}\times\Delta^1):p\to u(p)$ is $t$-cocartesian; thus the transport functor of $t$ along $0\to1$ is $u$, which is what it means for $t$ to be classified by $u$. Pullback along any simplex $\Delta^m\to\Delta^1$ is again a symmetric operadic family.

For every cocartesian fibration $q:E^\otimes\to O^\otimes$ which is a map of symmetric infinity-operads, let $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{inert}}_{/O^\otimes}(P^\otimes,E^\otimes)$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{inert}}_{/O^\otimes}(Q^\otimes,E^\otimes)$, and let $\mathcal L$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}_{/O^\otimes}(M_u^\otimes,E^\otimes)$ on family maps over $g$. Restriction along $j$ gives a map
$$R:\mathcal L\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal A)\times_{\mathcal A,\operatorname{ev}_1,u^*}\mathcal B$$
which lifts every simplex boundary, including dimension zero. It commutes exactly with the source restriction to $\mathcal A$. This is an assertion about the actual simplicial restriction, not merely an equivalence after passing to homotopy categories.

For every color $d$ of $Q^\otimes$, the source active slices have an equivalence
$$P^\otimes\times_{M_u^\otimes}(M_{u,\mathrm{act}}^\otimes)_{/d}\simeq P^\otimes\times_{Q^\otimes}(Q^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}})_{/d}.$$
It respects the source projection to $P^\otimes$ and, for every $H\in\mathcal L$ with $R(H)=(A,F,\eta)$, identifies the induced cocone of $H$ with the cocone whose component at $(p,\alpha:u(p)\to d)$ is $F(\alpha)\eta_p$, including its specified base cocone. Under these identifications $H$ satisfies the colorwise relative operadic left Kan condition if and only if these latter cocones are operadically $q$-colimiting. No colimit or Kan-extension hypothesis is imposed on $R(H)$.

source.place: Remark 3.1.3.15 and proof of Proposition 3.1.3.2, printed pp.346-348, with the cocartesian Grothendieck-cylinder model; compare Definition 2.3.2.10 and Proposition 2.3.2.11. The strengthened relative restriction and active-slice clauses are the explicit categorical-cylinder formulation of that construction, using cocartesian straightening (HTT 3.2.0.1) September 18, 2017 edition read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical operadic assertion.

proof.text: Form S_u=(P^⊗×Δ¹)⨿_{P^⊗×{1}}Q^⊗ degreewise. Its endpoint fibres are exactly P^⊗ and Q^⊗, even if u is not injective. The maps vu on the cylinder and v on Q agree on the glued end, and the maps to N(Fin_*) agree there as well; this defines both displayed base maps. A mixed n-simplex is represented by (a∈P_n, ε:[n]→[1] nonconstant), with operators applying u when all zero vertices disappear. Together with the pure endpoint simplices this is precisely the simplicial replacement G_[1](D), where D(0)=P, D(1)=Q and D(0→1)=u. No fibrancy or family assertion is inferred about this raw pushout.

source.place: Remark 3.1.3.15, raw mapping-cylinder pushout; simplicial replacement formula in the cited definition

proof.text: Construct the actual relative nerve N=R_[1](D) using [lem-cbc-strict-presentation-transport-representation], and write t₀:N→Δ¹. To make its data explicit, an n-simplex over ε is: if ε is constantly zero, a simplex a∈P_n; otherwise a simplex b∈Q_n and, when the initial zero block Z is nonempty, a simplex a:Δ^Z→P with b|Z=u(a). Every smaller subset in the relative-nerve formula is the restriction of a or b, so these data give exactly that formula. They define a simplicial map h:N→Q by ua in the pure-zero case and b otherwise. Thus h|P=u and h|Q=id exactly. Put π₀=(Fin_*∘h,t₀) and g₀=vh. The relative-nerve theorem gives a cocartesian fibration t₀ with exact fibres P,Q, and the edges e_p:p→up (with Q-edge id_up) are cocartesian. Its canonical map i:S_u=G_[1](D)→N is over both bases and is identity on each endpoint. For x∈Q, the cocartesian mapping criterion gives e_p^*:Map_Q(up,x)≃Map_N(p,x): the relevant base mapping spaces Δ¹(1,1), Δ¹(0,1) are both points. Applying h composes this equivalence with the identity because h(e_p)=id. Hence h induces the inverse equivalence Map_N(p,x)≃Map_Q(up,x), naturally over Map_Fin(Fin p,Fin x). Same-endpoint mapping spaces are exactly those of P or Q; reverse-endpoint mapping spaces are empty. We will use this explicit cross-fibre calculation, rather than deduce operadic structure from straightening.

source.place: Remark 3.1.3.15; HTT §3.2.5 relative nerve, with the explicit mixed-simplex calculation

proof.text: Use the current horn-reversal and categorical-equivalence clauses of [lem-coef-simplicial-opposite-homotopy-calculus]: reversal sends Λ_i^n to Λ_{n-i}^n, preserves inner fibrations and quasicategories, and reflects categorical equivalences for arbitrary simplicial sets. Reverse vertices. The formula for S_u in Step 1 becomes the mapping simplex of Q^op←P^op in [lem-coef-cartesian-mapping-simplex-presentation]. The horn definitions interchange cocartesian and cartesian edges, so t₀^op is cartesian and i^op takes each degenerate-fibre transition to a cartesian edge, by Step 2 and [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Apply [lem-cbc-cartesian-mapping-simplex-comparison] with n=1, K=Δ¹ and E the degenerate base edges. The endpoint maps are identities. The source marking is flat. The target marking is precisely the equivalences: an equivalence in N lies in an endpoint, and the relative-nerve edge criterion identifies cocartesian edges over identity base edges with equivalences in that endpoint. Thus (i^op)^flat→(N^op)^natural is an absolute marked weak equivalence. The existing [lem-coef-marked-flat-categorical-equivalence-test] gives that i^op is a categorical equivalence, without requiring S_u fibrant. Apply its categorical-equivalence reflection clause to i, whose source S_u need not be a quasicategory, to conclude that i is a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Definition 3.2.2.6 and Proposition 3.2.2.7(2), printed pp.180-181; apply the existing universal mapping-simplex comparison after reversing vertices.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-endpoint-fixed-inner-horn-refinement] to i:S_u→N over Δ¹. Step 3 supplies the categorical equivalence. The relative-nerve theorem of [lem-cbc-strict-presentation-transport-representation] supplies the quasicategory N and inner fibration t₀, with endpoint fibres P,Q and identity endpoint maps. Its subset-indexed formula uses sets in the universe of P,Q, so N is small. The refinement yields S_u --j→ M --k→ N with exact endpoint fibres, j degreewise injective and a categorical equivalence, and k a trivial Joyal fibration. The Joyal characterizations and functor-cone calculus give equivalences on mapping spaces for k; these will transfer the mapping-space squares below. The construction is independent of O.

source.place: Agent construction refining HA Remark 3.1.3.15 to an endpoint-fixed monomorphism, using mixed inner horns only; HTT §§2.2.5,2.4.6

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-relative-nerve-symmetric-family] to the strict diagram D(0)=P^⊗, D(1)=Q^⊗, D(0→1)=u over N(Fin_*). Its transitions preserve inert edges by the hypothesis that u is an operad map. Its subset-indexed construction is exactly N of Step 2 and its pointed-map coordinate is Fin_*∘h. The lemma proves that π₀:N→N(Fin_*)×Δ¹ is a symmetric operadic family, including categorical fibrancy, globally cocartesian inert lifts and all Segal squares. It also includes zero arity and all order-map pullbacks, which Step 6 uses.

source.place: HA Definition 2.3.2.10 and Remark 3.1.3.15; direct verification of mixed inner horns, inert lifts and the cross-fibre Segal square

proof.text: Set π=π₀k, t=t₀k and g=vhk. These agree on j(S_u) with the originally prescribed maps, on the nose. Since k and π₀ are categorical fibrations their composite is one (compose their diagonal lifts). The natural mapping-space equivalences induced by k transfer every square of the cocartesian mapping criterion and every incoming Segal square from N to M, with the same base. Consequently the given endpoint inert edges are π-cocartesian and the family axioms hold for M. Similarly t is an inner fibration, and the edges j({p}×Δ¹) are t-cocartesian because k maps them to e_p; along identity base edges use identities. These give a lift of every edge in Δ¹ from every object, so t is a cocartesian fibration with the specified transport u. An inert edge of M lies in an endpoint, since its Δ¹-edge is an equivalence. Restricting a π-cocartesian edge to endpoint tests makes it endpoint-cocartesian; conversely every endpoint inert cocartesian edge was proved π-cocartesian. Thus the inert edges of M are exactly the inert edges in P and Q. Their images under g are v u and v of those edges, hence inert in O, so g is a family map. For completeness check arbitrary simplex base change β:Δ^m→Δ¹ without assuming strict pullbacks preserve homotopy pullbacks. The pullback N_β is exactly the relative nerve for the strict diagram [m]→[1]→sSet, by its simplex formula. Its vertex values are P or Q, its nonidentity transition functors are identities or u. For vertices a≤b, its mapping spaces are Map_P, Map_Q or Map_Q(u−,−) according to these three cases; for a>b they are empty. The mixed-horn argument and all inert and Segal squares of Step 5 therefore apply unchanged, with the [m] mapping spaces either a point or empty. The pullback k_β:M_β→N_β still lifts all injections, so is a trivial Joyal fibration and induces the same mapping-space equivalences. Transferring the squares as above proves M_β is a family, including constant and degenerate β and m=0.

source.place: HA Definition 2.3.2.10, Proposition 2.3.2.11 and Remark 3.1.3.15; explicit transfer along the endpoint-identity trivial fibration and simplex pullback calculation

proof.text: Let T=Fun(Δ¹,A)×_{A,ev₁,u*}B. Degreewise maps S_u×Δ^n→E over its prescribed O-map are exactly a P×Δ¹×Δ^n diagram and a Q×Δ^n diagram agreeing on P×{1}×Δ^n. Requiring endpoint functors to preserve inert edges identifies their full simplicial subset with T: since A is full on inert-preserving functors, an n-simplex in Fun(Δ¹,A) requires precisely that its vertex functors on P are inert-preserving. By Step 6, a map M→E is a family map exactly when its two endpoint restrictions preserve inert edges. Therefore L is exactly the inverse image of T under the unrestricted simplicial restriction Fun_/O(M,E)→Fun_/O(S_u,E), including every higher simplex. For a square ∂Δ^n→L over Δ^n→T, transpose the two maps to the glued domain (M×∂Δ^n)⨿_{S_u×∂Δ^n}(S_u×Δ^n)→E over the fixed map g on M×Δ^n. The inclusion of that domain into M×Δ^n is j□(∂Δ^n→Δ^n), a degreewise injection and categorical equivalence by [lem-coef-joyal-cartesian-pushout-product]. The hypothesis on q makes it a Joyal fibration by [lem-coef-cocartesian-joyal-fibration]. Lift this precise square. The filler restricts to the prescribed inert-preserving endpoint functors at each vertex, so is a Δ^n simplex of L, and it gives the required exact boundary lift of R. For n=0 the same argument has empty boundary and gives a lift of every vertex of T. Restriction commutes literally with the source evaluation to A. All maps and transformations were over the fixed O-map throughout; when q=id_O there is just the forced map over g, so the previously proposed extra nonidentity unary transformation is not an object of T. No left Kan or colimit condition occurs in this argument.

source.place: HA Remark 3.1.3.15; HTT Corollary 2.2.5.4 and the categorical-fibration lifting property; NOT the source-only HA Lemma 3.1.3.16

proof.text: Fix a color d∈Q. The functor w=hk:M→Q fixes Q, restricts to u on P, preserves the pointed map of every simplex, and induces the equivalences Map_M(p,d)≃Map_Q(up,d) calculated in Steps 2 and 4. It therefore induces an actual simplicial map w_d between the two displayed source-projected active slices. For precise detection of its equivalence take the common source base P_act. The wide active subcategories of M,Q,P are quasicategories: an inner horn fills over its pointed-map simplex, and active pointed maps are closed under composition. The slice projection for M_act or Q_act is a right fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]; its pullback to P_act is one because each right-horn lifting square is the original square after projection. A simplex in either slice whose every arrow to d is active has active source edges: if α and αβ are active pointed maps, then β cannot send a nonbasepoint to the basepoint. Thus these pullbacks are exactly the slices in the statement, with their actual source projections, not smaller diagrams. Their fibres at p are the active unions of components of Map_M(p,d) and Map_Q(up,d). The pointed-map spaces in N(Fin_*) are discrete; the mapping-space equivalence induced by w is over them and hence restricts to an equivalence on each such union, including the empty union. Apply the explicit fibrewise-equivalence criterion for maps of right fibrations in [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. It gives an inverse with simplicial homotopies over P_act for the specified map w_d. Forgetting to P proves the required equivalence over P, retaining all higher simplices. This supplies the criterion missing from the returned pointwise-only argument.

source.place: HA Remark 3.1.3.15 and proof of Proposition 3.1.3.2; HTT Corollary 2.2.3.13 / right-fibration fibrewise detection, applied to active source slices

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-relative-nerve-cylinder-contraction] to the factorization i=kj. It gives Θ:id_M→incl_Q w, fixed on Q, with Θ_p=j({p}×Δ¹) and wΘ constant. For H∈L put F=H|Q and η=HΘ|P; this is exactly the transformation in R(H), not an arbitrary one. The lemma identifies the tautological cocone with the cocone of components F(α)η_p pulled back along w_d, retaining the entire naturality prism. Take B=N(Fin_*) and b the structure map of Q: its active edge class restricts this comparison to the active slices. Taking instead b=v shows the comparison is over the specified O-base cocone since g=vw. Step 8 supplies an inverse equivalence of indexing quasicategories over P. Precomposition with that equivalence and the pointwise cocone equivalence induce equivalences on all mapping spaces by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. After every fixed concatenation by Z the same holds, and [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] identifies the horizontal maps with composition by the compared cocones. Consequently the four corners and composition paths of the defining q-colimit squares are identified. Apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] to these squares. One is a homotopy pullback exactly when the other is, for every Z and target color W, including the empty tuple and empty active slice. By [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family] this is the asserted equivalence of colorwise conditions, without any prior colimit hypothesis.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N5-bf4071338 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item's 9 steps, the 3 new nodes, the statements of all 22 cited nodes, and the unit record. Structure is clean: proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, no cycle, nothing merged, every step is at most 1955 characters, and no SGA is cited. The item statement is unchanged and it is not a target. Step 3 is correct: S_u reversed is the mapping simplex M^m(Q^op<-P^op); the cartesian mapping-simplex comparison with K=Δ¹ and E the degenerate edges gives a flat-to-natural marked weak equivalence; the marked-flat test then gives i^op as a categorical equivalence, and the current opposite statement reflects this to i. The endpoint-fixed refinement is true: pure horns are solved inside the fixed fibres; deleting an inner vertex of a mixed horn leaves a mixed face, so no endpoint simplex is added; the resulting map is an inner fibration and an isofibration, hence a trivial Joyal fibration by two-out-of-three. The family node is true: inner horns fill in D(σ(n)), mapping spaces are Map_{D(b)}(D(a→b)x,y) or empty, the r=0 square is ∅→pt over ∅→pt, and the order-map pullback formula is literal. The contraction node is true: θ has the explicit formula with coordinate ε∨δ and Q-datum h(x); Θ is a lift against k with all four overlaps checked; η=HΘ|=Hj| is exactly the η of R(H); the prism gives H(β)≃F(wβ)η_p; and bwΘ=bw·pr gives base compatibility. Small cases tested: u=id, P=∅, noninjective u, m=0. No duplicates found among the filtered/relative Joyal factorizations, the relative-nerve and family-calculus nodes, or the prism/cone nodes, and none restates a clause of the item. Steps 5–9 check against their cited statements: w|_P=u, active cancellation, right-fibration fibrewise detection, the j□∂Δ^n lift against the Joyal fibration q, and homotopy-pullback invariance. I accept the three sk-prop-sf-cbc tool_uses. HA and HTT are not archived locally and are recorded as WANTED.
